evidence.title: Redwood reports simulated control evaluations predicted LinuxArena safety with 3.6-percentage-point RMSE versus 10.1 for BashArena at 5% audit budget across five monitors.
evidence.observation: Redwood reports simulated control evaluations predicted LinuxArena safety with 3.6-percentage-point RMSE versus 10.1 for BashArena at 5% audit budget across five monitors. Simulated attack briefings improved detection on held-out executed attacks.

source_locations.SRC-030: Abstract; Section 3.7; Section 4 Limitations and discussion; author blog opening limitations

evidence.limitations: Validation is LinuxArena-specific, not deployment proof. Section 4 assumes a trusted simulator: collusion could hide success and inflate safety. Greater apparent realism did not necessarily improve transfer; long-horizon multi-agent coverage remains absent in the author blog.
evidence.open_questions: Generalization outside inspected settings and completeness/authenticity of underlying traces remain unestablished by the Commons.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed bounded finding; publication inclusion does not certify truth or completeness. arXiv, Redwood blog and authorSubstack are same study; not independent replication. Relevant to mirrored/simulated logs without claiming operational manipulation occurred. No matching source or underlying case found among baseline v0.4.1 SRC-001–018 / CASE-001–017; recurring report mentions merge into this candidate, not corroboration.
evidence.dispute_status: Bounded correction checks; known limitations retained, no absence guarantee
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.
